note: Attacker-controlled raw DNS packet bytes (data/data_len) enter the protocol decoder and are forwarded to fr_dns_decode.

code: slen = decode_record(ctx, cursor, attr_dns_rr, p, end - p, packet_ctx, packet + 6);
note: Answer-section RRs are decoded per the ancount field; p points at the first RR after the 12-byte header with end - p bytes remaining.

code:
slen = fr_struct_from_network(ctx, cursor, attr, p, end - p, true,
					      packet_ctx, decode_value_trampoline, NULL);
note: The RR bytes are handed to the generic struct decoder; fixed members (name label 1B, type 2B, class 2B, ttl 4B) consume 9 of the 10 RR bytes, leaving exactly 1 byte of RDATA.

code:
slen = fr_struct_from_network(child_ctx, &child_cursor, child, p, end - p, nested,
					      decode_ctx, decode_value, decode_tlv);
note: The key field 'type' (value 1 = A record) selects the length-prefixed substruct dns-rr-a, and the nested decode is invoked with only the remaining 1 byte of RDATA.
Root cause: for a length-prefixed substruct the decoder enters this branch and reads a 16-bit length header without first verifying that at least two bytes (data_len >= 2) are available.
Sink: when only one byte remains in the input buffer, p[1] reads one byte past the end of the heap buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow.
